domainName.description: Specifies the corresponding domain name for a whois entry.

registrarInfo.description: Specifies registrar info that would be returned from a registrar lookup.

remarks.description: Specifies any remarks associated with this Whois entry.

serverName.description: Specifies the corresponding server name for a whois entry. This usually corresponds to a name server lookup.

sponsoringRegistrar.description: Specifies the name of the sponsoring registrar for a domain.

status.description: Specifies a list of statuses for a given Whois entry.

updatedDate.description: Specifies the date in which the registered domain information was last updated.

WindowsCriticalSection.description: A Windows critical section is a Windows object that provides synchronization similar to that provided by a mutex object, except that a critical section can be used only by the threads of a single process. Critical section objects cannot be shared across processes. Event, mutex, and semaphore objects can also be used in a single-process application, but critical section objects provide a slightly faster, more efficient mechanism for mutual-exclusion synchronization (a processor-specific test and set instruction). Like a mutex object, a critical section object can be owned by only one thread at a time, which makes it useful for protecting a shared resource from simultaneous access. Unlike a mutex object, there is no way to tell whether a critical section has been abandoned. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sync/critical-section-objects]

WindowsFilemapping.description: A Windows file mapping is the association of a file's contents with a portion of the virtual address space of a process within a Windows operating system. The system creates a file mapping object (also known as a section object) to maintain this association. A file view is the portion of virtual address space that a process uses to access the file's contents. File mapping allows the process to use both random input and output (I/O) and sequential I/O. It also allows the process to work efficiently with a large data file, such as a database, without having to map the whole file into memory. Multiple processes can also use memory-mapped files to share data. Processes read from and write to the file view using pointers, just as they would with dynamically allocated memory. The use of file mapping improves efficiency because the file resides on disk, but the file view resides in memory.[based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/memory/file-mapping]

Network sharing is made possible by inter-process communication over the network. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shared_resource]

WindowsPEBinaryFileFacet.description: A Windows PE binary file facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a Windows portable executable (PE) file.

characteristics.description: Specifies the flags that indicate the file’s characteristics.

fileHeaderHashes.description: Specifies any hashes that were computed for the file header.

impHash.description: Specifies the special import hash, or ‘imphash’, calculated for the PE Binary based on its imported libraries and functions.

machine.description: Specifies the type of target machine.

numberOfSections.description: Specifies the number of sections in the PE binary, as a non-negative integer.

numberOfSymbols.description: Specifies the number of entries in the symbol table of the PE binary, as a non-negative integer.

optionalHeader.description: Specifies the PE optional header of the PE binary.

peType.description: Specifies the type of the PE binary.

pointerToSymbolTable.description: Specifies the file offset of the COFF symbol table.

sections.description: Specifies metadata about the sections in the PE file.

sizeOfOptionalHeader.description: Specifies the size of the optional header of the PE binary.

timeDateStamp.description: Specifies the time when the PE binary was created.

type.description: The class the thing is an instance of, as the class's CURIE, such as uco-observable:File.

WindowsPEFileHeader.description: A Windows PE file header is a grouping of characteristics unique to the 'header' of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of a collection of metadata about the overall nature and structure of the file.

timeDateStamp.description: Specifies the time when the PE binary was created.

type.description: The class the thing is an instance of, as the class's CURIE, such as uco-observable:File.

WindowsPEFileHeader.title: WindowsPEFileHeader

WindowsPEOptionalHeader.description: A Windows PE optional header is a grouping of characteristics unique to the 'optional header' of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of a collection of metadata about the executable code structure of the file.

addressOfEntryPoint.description: Specifies the address of the entry point relative to the image base when the executable is loaded into memory.

baseOfCode.description: Specifies the address that is relative to the image base of the beginning-of-code section when it is loaded into memory.

checksum.description: Specifies the checksum of the PE binary.

dllCharacteristics.description: Specifies the flags that characterize the PE binary.

fileAlignment.description: Specifies the factor (in bytes) that is used to align the raw data of sections in the image file.

imageBase.description: Specifies the address that is relative to the image base of the beginning-of-data section when it is loaded into memory.

magic.description: Specifies the value that indicates the type of the PE binary.

majorImageVersion.description: Specifies the major version number of the image.

majorLinkerVersion.description: Specifies the linker major version number.

majorOSVersion.description: Specifies the major version number of the required operating system.

majorSubsystemVersion.description: Specifies the major version number of the subsystem.

minorImageVersion.description: Specifies the minor version number of the image.

minorLinkerVersion.description: Specifies the linker minor version number.

minorOSVersion.description: Specifies the minor version number of the required operating system.

minorSubsystemVersion.description: Specifies the minor version number of the subsystem.

numberOfRVAAndSizes.description: Specifies the number of data-directory entries in the remainder of the optional header.

sectionAlignment.description: Specifies the alignment (in bytes) of PE sections when they are loaded into memory.

sizeOfCode.description: Specifies the size of the code (text) section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

sizeOfHeaders.description: Specifies the combined size of the MS-DOS, PE header, and section headers, rounded up a multiple of the value specified in the file_alignment header.

sizeOfHeapCommit.description: Specifies the size of the local heap space to commit.

sizeOfHeapReserve.description: Specifies the size of the local heap space to reserve.

sizeOfImage.description: Specifies the size, in bytes, of the image, including all headers, as the image is loaded in memory.

sizeOfInitializedData.description: Specifies the size of the initialized data section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

sizeOfStackCommit.description: Specifies the size of the stack to commit.

sizeOfStackReserve.description: Specifies the size of the stack to reserve.

sizeOfUninitializedData.description: Specifies the size of the uninitialized data section. If there are multiple such sections, this refers to the sum of the sizes of each section.

subsystem.description: Specifies the subsystem (e.g., GUI, device driver, etc.) that is required to run this image.

type.description: The class the thing is an instance of, as the class's CURIE, such as uco-observable:File.

win32VersionValue.description: Specifies the reserved win32 version value.

WindowsPESection.description: A Windows PE section is a grouping of characteristics unique to a specific default or custom-defined region of a Windows PE (Portable Executable) file, consisting of an individual portion of the actual executable content of the file delineated according to unique purpose and memory protection requirements.

entropy.description: Shannon entropy (a measure of randomness) of the data.

hashes.description: Specifies any hashes computed over the section.

name.description: The name of a particular concept characterization.

size.description: Specifies the size of the section, in bytes.

type.description: The class the thing is an instance of, as the class's CURIE, such as uco-observable:File.

WindowsTaskFacet.description: A Windows Task facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a Windows Task (a process that is scheduled to execute on a Windows operating system by the Windows Task Scheduler). [based on http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381311(v=vs.85).aspx]

account.description: Specifies the account referenced in an event log entry or used to run the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381228(v=vs.85).aspx.

accountLogonType.description: Specifies the security logon method required to run the tasks associated with the account. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa383013(v=vs.85).aspx.

accountRunLevel.description: Specifies the permission level of the account that the task will be run at.

actionList.description: Specifies a list of actions to be performed by the scheduled task.

application.description: The application associated with this object.

exitCode.description: Specifies the last exit code of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381245(v=vs.85).aspx.

flags.description: Specifies any flags that modify the behavior of the scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381248(v=vs.85).aspx.

imageName.description: Specifies the image name for the task.

maxRunTime.description: Specifies the maximum run time of the scheduled task before terminating, in milliseconds. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381874(v=vs.85).aspx.

mostRecentRunTime.description: Specifies the most recent run date/time of this scheduled task. See also: http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa381254(v=vs.85).aspx.
